question: If knowledge arises in an all-pervading self, why would life not be established in all bodies and even in pots and the like?
premises: The opponent allows knowledge to arise in an all-pervading self.
An all-pervading self is present everywhere.
The same reasoning would extend life or sentience beyond individual bodies.
inference: The all-pervading-self account overgeneralizes and absurdly implies life in all bodies and inert objects.
plain_english: If it has arisen in that way, why would life not be established in all bodies? And by that very reasoning, why would pots and the like not also be alive?
